access-audit-trails: Connect who requested data, what was authorized, and what access actually occurred, preserving enough evidence to investigate activity across systems.
accumulating-snapshots: Keep one row per process instance and update its milestones as work progresses, making completion status and elapsed times easier to analyze.
additive-schema-evolution: Introduce new fields alongside existing ones while preserving the meanings current consumers rely on, with explicit rules for missing values and migration.
adjacency-lists: Store each hierarchy node’s immediate parent as a reference, keeping updates compact while reconstructing longer paths through traversal.
aggregate-fact-tables: Store summaries at an explicit coarser level of detail to accelerate recurring queries, while retaining detailed data for questions the summaries cannot answer.
allowed-lateness: Retain window state for a defined event-time horizon so accepted late records can revise results before routine correction stops.
as-of-joins: Match each observation to a reference record using an explicit time-relative rule, such as the latest eligible version at or before the observation.
associative-entities: Give a many-to-many relationship its own records, identifying the participants and providing a place for the relationship’s attributes, identity, and lifecycle.
atomic-publication: Make a complete, validated data release visible in one switch, so readers use a coherent version rather than a partially updated dataset.
backpressure: Slow or pause upstream admission when downstream work cannot keep up, using feedback to bound buffering instead of letting queues grow without control.
bitemporal-records: Track when information applies in the business and when the system recorded it, supporting queries with separate business-time and knowledge-time cutoffs.
bounded-contexts: Give each business model an explicit boundary for its terms and rules, then connect models through deliberate mappings rather than assuming shared meanings.
bounded-retries: Limit retry attempts, elapsed time, and extra load, then send unresolved work to an explicit outcome instead of retrying indefinitely.
bounded-stream-stream-joins: Match events across streams by key and an explicit time relationship, using progress and lateness policies to bound how long possible matches are retained.
bridge-tables: Represent relationships where a measurement belongs to several categories or participants, with explicit allocation when totals must add up without duplication.
broadcast-small-inputs: Copy a small, versioned input to each worker so it can join or enrich its larger local input without redistributing that larger dataset.
business-invariant-checks: Check relationships that must hold in the business, such as balanced amounts or valid lifecycle transitions, to catch errors that structural validation misses.
calendar-dimensions: Store agreed calendar, fiscal, and business-day attributes for dates, so reports use consistent period definitions instead of repeating date logic.
canonical-mapping: Translate source-specific structures, codes, units, and meanings into an explicit shared model, preserving the context needed to explain each mapping.
capture-lineage-at-transformation: Record the actual input versions and transformation used for each output while the job runs, supporting investigation, impact analysis, and controlled rebuilding.
checkpoint-and-resume: Save a durable recovery point that aligns input progress, processing state, and recoverable output, allowing interrupted work to resume safely.
chunked-snapshotting: Divide a large snapshot into tracked, bounded ranges so work can be retried or parallelized independently under a defined consistency and completion policy.
circuit-breakers: Temporarily stop calls to an unhealthy dependency, then use limited probes to decide when traffic may resume, protecting resources during extended failures.
claim-check: Store a large payload separately and send a durable reference through the message channel, keeping that exact payload version retrievable by authorized consumers.
classification-based-retention: Assign retention rules by data class and a documented start event, then account for holds and disposal conditions before removing records.
closure-tables: Store ancestor–descendant pairs explicitly, including self-links, so hierarchy queries can use direct lookups at the cost of more storage and maintenance.
cluster-related-records: Place records commonly read together near one another in storage, reducing candidate blocks while retaining exact row filtering where mixed records remain.
co-located-joins: Coordinate the placement of related inputs so matching rows reach the same join task, avoiding repeated redistribution when the engine recognizes compatible layouts.
columnar-storage: Store values by column so analytical queries can read and compress the fields they need without routinely loading unrelated data.
compatibility-checks-in-delivery: Test proposed data-interface changes against the producer, reader, and retained-data versions that must coexist before allowing rollout.
compensating-actions: Recover a partially completed workflow through explicit, scoped actions that correct its business effects, without undoing unrelated work or assuming a global rollback.
composite-keys: Use a combination of columns as one identifier, with uniqueness and references checked against the complete combination.
conformed-dimensions: Use consistent identities, descriptive attributes, and calendar meanings across business processes so their independently summarized results can be compared reliably.
conformed-facts: Align measurement definitions, units, scope, and timing across sources, making comparisons meaningful while keeping the rules for combining values explicit.
consistent-snapshot-reads: Keep related reads on one stable visibility boundary, producing a coherent view of the source while other transactions continue changing it.
consumer-driven-contract-tests: Let consumers define executable expectations for the interfaces they actually use, then verify those expectations against provider changes before rollout.
controlled-vocabularies: Define agreed categories with stable codes, clear meanings, and recognized labels, so systems classify and exchange data consistently without merging distinct concepts.
covering-indexes: Include the values a query needs in its index so fewer table-row fetches are needed, while accounting for engine-specific visibility checks.
cursor-based-incremental-extraction: Resume extraction from a source-provided cursor, saving progress only after the page is durable and handling duplicates when a failed attempt is replayed.
data-minimization: Collect, process, and share only the information needed for a defined purpose, limiting unnecessary detail, identification, duplication, and continued retention.
data-aware-dependencies: Start dependent work only when its specific inputs and readiness conditions are satisfied, rather than relying on the clock or upstream job success alone.
dataset-deprecation-and-retirement: End a dataset’s service through announced deprecation, consumer migration, and explicit retirement, with separate decisions for retained history and disposal.
dead-letter-queues: Move work that normal processing cannot complete into a durable recovery channel, retaining identity and failure context for accountable diagnosis and controlled reprocessing.
declare-the-grain: Define exactly what one row represents before choosing keys, measurements, and joins, so calculations do not silently mix observations at different levels of detail.
deduplicate-explicit-winner: Group competing records by their intended identity and select one whole row using a documented, deterministic precedence rule, with explicit handling of unresolved conflicts.
degenerate-dimensions: Keep useful business identifiers, such as invoice numbers, on measurement rows when no descriptive attributes justify a separate dimension table.
deletion-propagation: Carry an approved deletion through relevant copies and derived data, track outcomes at each destination, and prevent older inputs from recreating removed information.
deletion-tombstones: Represent deletions with retained identity and ordering information, allowing downstream removal and rejection of older updates during the supported replay horizon.
deterministic-transformations: Produce the same defined result from the same complete inputs and rules, making time, reference versions, ordering, and other hidden dependencies explicit.
distinguish-missing-unknown-inapplicable: Record why a value is absent, distinguishing missing evidence from unknown information and legitimate inapplicability so validation and calculations preserve the intended meaning.
distribution-monitoring: Monitor how values are spread across a dataset, revealing shifts in ranges, categories, or missingness that normal row counts and averages can conceal.
document-aggregates: Group a bounded set of owned data in one document so a meaningful business unit can be read and updated together.
domain-owned-data-products: Give the business domain ongoing responsibility for a published dataset’s meaning, quality, operation, and support, so consumers have an accountable data product.
drill-across: Summarize each business process separately by shared reporting categories, then align the summaries to compare results without multiplying detailed records.
dynamic-masking: Choose the value displayed at query time according to the caller’s policy, while retaining the stored original and protecting access to it.
early-results-with-corrections: Publish provisional results before all expected data arrives, then issue identifiable revisions that consumers can apply correctly despite retries or out-of-order delivery.
effective-dated-records: Store when a value or rule applies in the business, supporting historical lookups and scheduled changes independently of when the record was saved.
end-to-end-canary-records: Send recognizable test records through the real pipeline and verify the expected result at the consumer, detecting failures that individual job checks can miss.
entity-resolution: Decide which records describe the same real-world entity by comparing evidence, managing uncertainty, and retaining the reasons for accepted or rejected matches.
event-sourcing: Make accepted business events the authoritative record and reconstruct state by applying them in order, keeping replay separate from repeated external actions.
event-time-processing: Group and evaluate events by when they happened, with explicit rules for delayed arrivals and corrections.
expand-migrate-contract: Introduce a replacement alongside the old interface, migrate data and consumers, then remove the old representation after verifying that dependencies have moved.
explicit-data-contracts: Make producer–consumer agreements explicit about structure, meaning, units, row definitions, and operational expectations, so readable data is also interpreted correctly.
exponential-backoff-with-jitter: Increase retry wait limits after failures and randomize individual waits, reducing repeated load and synchronized request bursts during recovery.
factless-fact-tables: Record occurrences or expected relationships without requiring a numeric measure, supporting counts of participation and comparisons between expected and recorded activity.
federated-governance: Let domain teams govern their own data within shared agreements for interoperability and protection, with clear responsibility for common rules and exceptions.
freshness-monitoring: Measure how current usable data is against a timeliness objective, tracing delay through source progress, processing, publication, and consumption.
full-snapshot-extraction: Copy every record within a declared source scope on each run, establishing a complete baseline whose consistency and completion must be verified.
golden-records: Assemble a governed profile from records linked to the same entity, selecting values by explicit authority rules and preserving their sources.
graph-relationships: Represent entities as nodes and meaningful connections as edges, so queries can follow dependencies, relationships, and paths across several steps.
half-open-time-intervals: Include an interval’s start and exclude its end, so adjoining periods share a boundary without counting that instant twice.
historical-restatement: Recalculate previously reported periods when evidence or rules change, publishing identifiable revisions while retaining enough history to explain earlier reports.
horizontal-sharding: Distribute rows across independently operated shards and route requests to their owners, increasing capacity while making cross-shard work and resharding explicit responsibilities.
hot-cold-tiering: Place frequently accessed data on fast storage and less-active history on cheaper tiers, with explicit query, restore, and retrieval-cost expectations.
hybrid-slowly-changing-dimensions: Combine dimension-history techniques so the same measurements can be grouped by both historical attributes and current classifications, with each perspective explicit.
idempotent-writes: Make repeated attempts at the same logical write produce the intended effect once, so retries can resolve uncertain outcomes without duplication.
identity-crosswalks: Maintain links backed by evidence between identifiers for the same entity, allowing systems to retain local IDs while supporting reconciliation across boundaries.
incremental-replacement: Transfer responsibility from an old system to its replacement one coherent slice at a time, verifying each handover while keeping ownership unambiguous.
incremental-transformations: Maintain an existing transformation result by processing changes and all affected outputs, including corrections and removals that reach beyond newly arrived rows.
inferred-dimension-members: Create a stable placeholder for a known entity before its descriptive details arrive, then complete that same member without changing the facts’ reference.
junk-dimensions: Combine small categorical attributes into a reusable table of valid profiles, replacing scattered flags with one reference while controlling combination growth.
keep-previous-values-scd-type-3: Keep a previous attribute value beside the current value for limited comparison, accepting that older changes and complete event-time history are not preserved.
keyset-pagination: Continue a paged query after the last complete ordering key, reducing skipped-row scanning while requiring a stable ordering and explicit consistency policy.
leases-with-fencing-tokens: Assign temporary ownership with a lease and increasing tokens; the protected destination rejects an older owner after accepting a newer token.
location-aware-placement: Constrain where data is stored, processed, and recovered, including temporary copies and logs, so placement follows an explicit geographic policy.
log-based-change-data-capture: Read committed inserts, updates, and deletions from database logs, preserving the ordering and transaction boundaries needed to maintain downstream data.
lookback-recalculation: Repeatedly rebuild a recent historical range to absorb late changes, while routing corrections beyond that recovery horizon to a separate backfill.
make-units-explicit: Carry units, scales, and measurement meanings with numerical values, then convert compatible quantities before combining them in calculations.
manifest-based-file-ingestion: Declare an ingestible batch with an explicit list of immutable files and validation details, so consumers know exactly which complete set to process.
materialized-paths: Store each hierarchy node’s ancestry as a path, making branch searches and breadcrumbs direct while requiring descendant paths to change when a branch moves.
materialized-views: Store a query’s derived result for reuse, with explicit maintenance and freshness rules that keep consumers aware of when the stored answer is valid.
merge-and-upsert: Match incoming records to stored identities and apply explicit insert, update, and delete rules, rejecting stale or conflicting changes according to policy.
metadata-driven-pipelines: Describe supported pipeline variations in versioned specifications interpreted by reusable execution logic, keeping configuration separate from checkpoints and other runtime progress.
microbatch-processing: Process a stream as successive bounded batches with recorded input ranges, allowing batch-style execution and recovery while keeping batch cadence separate from event-time windows.
mini-dimensions: Move frequently changing profile attributes into a separate table of combinations, and let each fact record the profile observed at its event.
model-around-business-processes: Organize analytical data around distinct business activities, so each process keeps meaningful observations and measurements while shared context connects the results.
model-lifecycle-states-explicitly: Represent meaningful process stages and allowed transitions explicitly, tying actions such as approval or publication to the state and revision they actually apply to.
named-dataset-stewardship: Assign each important dataset a current, discoverable steward who coordinates questions, quality decisions, and escalation across business and technical responsibilities.
namespace-identifiers: Carry an identifier’s assigning scope with its local value, so matching values from different systems or environments are not mistaken for the same identity.
natural-keys: Identify records using business-recognized attributes whose combinations are unique within a defined scope, while accounting for change and reuse.
normalized-relations: Store facts according to the attributes they depend on, reducing repeated updates and contradictory copies across related records.
operational-service-objectives: Define measurable targets for data-service behavior, evaluate them over a stated period, and use the allowed shortfall to guide operational decisions.
overlapping-extraction-windows: Reread a bounded interval before the saved extraction boundary to recover delayed visibility, merging repeated records and providing another route for changes outside that interval.
overwrite-attributes-scd-type-1: Replace an attribute in its existing dimension row when the model needs the corrected or current value, accepting that earlier classifications are overwritten.
parallel-run-comparison: Compare two implementations using matched inputs, conditions, and output identities, revealing differences that equal row counts or grand totals can conceal.
partition-by-access-pattern: Choose partition boundaries to match important filters, writes, and retention operations, enabling the system to skip or manage whole relevant slices.
partition-replacement: Rebuild the complete result for a bounded dataset slice and replace that slice together, preserving unaffected data and avoiding duplicate accumulation.
party-role-modeling: Separate a person or organization’s identity from its roles in particular relationships, allowing roles, counterparties, and effective dates to vary independently.
per-key-ordering: Apply events for each business key in their required sequence while allowing different keys to progress independently, coordinating routing and state changes.
periodic-snapshots: Record measurements at regular intervals, making historical balances and trends available while keeping each period’s observations distinct from business events.
policy-as-code: Express governing rules as versioned, testable code and connect their decisions to controlled actions on the exact data or candidate being evaluated.
predicate-projection-pushdown: Filter rows and select required columns near the source, reducing transferred and processed data while preserving query meaning and update semantics.
preserve-raw-inputs: Retain incoming data and its source context before interpretation, so parsing mistakes or changed business rules can be investigated through controlled reprocessing.
progressive-refinement: Improve captured inputs through explicit stages of validation, standardization, enrichment, and summarization, making changes in trust, meaning, and detail traceable.
property-based-data-tests: Generate varied inputs to test general properties of a transformation, exposing edge cases that a fixed collection of examples may miss.
publication-quality-gates: Validate a specific candidate release before making it visible, binding checks to its exact inputs and version while preserving the previous release if validation fails.
publish-subscribe-distribution: Distribute published events to independent subscriptions, so several consumers can react separately while managing their own progress and repeated deliveries.
published-deprecation-windows: Give consumers a usable replacement, support commitments, and a clear retirement deadline, with checkpoints for migration readiness and published exception handling.
quality-gates: A check becomes a decision that holds, rejects, or advances a candidate, with incomplete evidence handled explicitly.
quarantine-invalid-records: Isolate records that cannot safely proceed, preserving their original content and failure context for investigation, correction, and controlled reprocessing.
read-replicas: Serve reads from additional database copies to share load, with explicit rules for replication lag and queries that must observe recent writes.
recorded-time-history: Preserve when the system recorded each version, so earlier queries can reproduce what that system knew at a chosen cutoff.
reference-data-enrichment: Attach context from a governed lookup dataset using explicit key, version, time, and missing-match rules, preserving the intended input row count.
referential-integrity-checks: Check that references resolve to the intended records using complete identities and the relevant historical or lifecycle rules.
relationships-with-attributes: Store roles, quantities, dates, and conditions on the particular relationship they describe, rather than attaching them incorrectly to either participant.
replayable-backfills: Define historical reruns with pinned scope, inputs, and processing versions, then validate and publish results through a repeatable recovery protocol that coordinates with live work.
representative-test-fixtures: Keep small, controlled examples of important processing conditions, including initial state and event order where relevant, with independently specified expected outcomes.
representative-text-fixtures: Preserve realistic text edge cases and exact expected interpretations, testing quoting, line breaks, Unicode, and embedded syntax that tidy sample strings miss.
reshape-at-boundaries: Change nested, relational, or reporting structures at explicit interfaces while preserving identity, row meaning, and measurement totals across representations.
result-caching: Reuse a computed answer only when its data version, query meaning, parameters, access scope, and freshness still satisfy the new request.
retain-original-values-scd-type-0: Preserve an attribute’s defined original value for stable baseline analysis, distinguishing the verified business starting point from the first value a pipeline happened to observe.
reusable-intermediate-models: Build focused intermediate datasets that several downstream models can reuse, with explicit row meaning and dependencies that reduce repeated or inconsistent transformation logic.
role-playing-dimensions: Use the same descriptive table in several named roles, such as order date and ship date, with each role linked and filtered independently.
row-and-column-level-access: Enforce which records a caller may access and which fields they may read, using the caller’s authorized context for the query.
run-ledgers: Record intended work, attempts, input versions, and verified output outcomes in a durable ledger, distinguishing uncertain results from confirmed failures or completion.
schema-registries: Keep versioned schema definitions available so each payload can be decoded with its writing schema and proposed changes checked against supported readers.
schema-validation-boundaries: Validate incoming records against an explicit structural contract before downstream processing relies on their fields, types, and required values.
secondary-access-paths: Maintain additional query-oriented routes to authoritative records, accelerating important lookups while defining how each route stays current and handles stale or missing candidates.
segmented-quality-checks: Evaluate data quality within meaningful groups as well as overall, so a large healthy segment cannot hide failures in a smaller one.
self-service-data-discovery: Publish searchable, maintained information that helps people find suitable data, understand its limits, and follow an appropriate access route before querying.
sensitive-data-segregation: Place sensitive details behind separately controlled storage or access boundaries, allowing ordinary workflows to use less-sensitive data without receiving the protected fields.
separate-backfill-from-live-processing: Give historical reruns separate checkpoints and resource budgets so they do not disrupt current processing, while coordinating how historical results replace or join live output.
separate-cleaning-business-logic: Give source preparation and business interpretation distinct steps, so cleaning preserves usable evidence while explicit business rules determine derived results.
separate-definitions-from-instances: Model shared specifications separately from the individual things or runs that follow them, allowing each instance to retain its own identity, state, and history.
separate-entities-from-events: Give continuing entities stable identities and record occurrences separately, so repeated events and changing current state do not erase or confuse business history.
separate-source-facts-from-derived-inter: Preserve source assertions separately from calculated classifications, retaining input and rule references so interpretations can change without rewriting their evidence.
session-windows: Group each key’s events into activity periods separated by a defined inactivity gap, allowing late events to extend or merge sessions under the retention policy.
shadow-pipelines: Run a candidate pipeline beside production on matched inputs, keeping its outputs and side effects isolated while collecting evidence before a possible handover.
shared-business-vocabulary: Agree on precise, scoped meanings for business terms and carry those meanings into models, transformations, reports, and tests.
shared-metric-definitions: Maintain a metric’s business meaning and reusable calculation together, aligning population, units, time, exclusions, and aggregation rules across consuming tools.
skew-splitting: Split an overloaded key or partition across parallel tasks, then combine results or arrange join matches so the original operation’s meaning is preserved.
sliding-windows: Calculate results over moving, usually overlapping time horizons, retaining context across reporting boundaries while recognizing that one event may contribute to several results.
small-file-compaction: Combine small files into fewer, larger files through a coordinated metadata update, preserving the logical rows, concurrent additions, and existing readers.
snapshot-then-stream: Coordinate a baseline snapshot with a source change stream, so existing data and subsequent committed changes meet at a defined boundary without gaps.
snowflake-schema: Separate descriptive hierarchy levels into linked tables, so shared categories can be maintained independently while each measurement row keeps its meaning.
source-to-target-reconciliation: Compare source and destination populations, identities, amounts, and expected transformations to detect missing, duplicated, or unexpectedly changed records.
stable-logical-interfaces: Keep a consistent dataset contract for consumers while changing the underlying storage or computation, verifying that meaning and observable behavior remain compatible.
standardize-at-staging: Standardize source-specific names, types, units, and codes once at staging, giving downstream models a consistent source representation before business interpretation.
star-schema: Put business measurements in a central fact table and connect descriptive lookup tables for consistent filtering, grouping, and reporting.
state-expiration: Remove working state when its defined retention or correctness horizon ends, bounding resource use while making the resulting limits explicit.
stateful-stream-deduplication: Remember event identities for a declared horizon and suppress repeated deliveries, coordinating retained state and outputs so recovery preserves the intended duplicate-handling guarantee.
store-additive-components: Retain totals, counts, and weighted components behind rates or averages so combined results can be calculated correctly rather than averaging incompatible summaries.
stream-table-enrichment: Attach reference attributes to streaming events using an explicit temporal rule, such as the latest available table state or a historical version valid at event time.
supertype-subtype-modeling: Share identity and common attributes across related kinds of entity, while giving each subtype the specific attributes and rules it needs.
surrogate-keys: Introduce an internal identifier for an entity or version, keeping references independent of the business attributes used to recognize it.
tokenization: Replace sensitive values with controlled substitutes so approved workflows can link records while access to originals and any recovery mapping remains restricted.
tolerant-readers: Accept permitted interface extensions while validating the fields and meanings needed for the task, reducing avoidable breakage without silently accepting incompatible data.
transaction-fact-tables: Store one row for each identifiable business occurrence, with the measurements and descriptive references that belong to that occurrence.
transactional-consume-process-publish: Commit outputs, processing state, and consumed-input progress within one supported transaction, so failures preserve or roll back those changes together.
transactional-inbox: Record message completion and its business changes in one database transaction, so redelivery can recognize work already completed.
transactional-outbox: Save an outgoing message with its business change in one database transaction, then relay committed messages with duplicate handling.
transformation-unit-tests: Run a specific transformation against controlled inputs and independently defined expected outputs, checking business behavior before changes reach larger datasets.
trigger-based-change-capture: Capture selected database changes in a local change table within the source transaction, then deliver those records downstream with explicit progress and retry handling.
tumbling-windows: Divide time into fixed, adjacent, nonoverlapping windows so each event timestamp belongs to one interval under an explicit boundary convention.
version-dimension-rows-scd-type-2: Preserve successive descriptions as separate dimension rows with validity intervals, linking each fact to the appropriate version for historical reporting.
version-transformation-logic: Identify and retain the transformation version that produced each output, supporting investigation, controlled backfills, and reproduction of earlier results.
versioned-dataset-interface: Give materially different dataset contracts separate, stable interfaces so consumers can migrate deliberately while routine data refreshes continue within each version.
vertical-partitioning: Separate frequently used fields from large or rarely needed fields, keeping routine reads narrow while preserving identity and version consistency across the split.
volume-monitoring: Monitor data quantities and their contributions against expectations, revealing unusual changes that successful jobs or stable overall totals can conceal.
watermarks: Use a source’s estimate or guarantee of event-time progress to decide when to publish window results and clean up retained state.
workload-isolation: Give live processing, backfills, and other workloads enforceable resource budgets and queues, limiting how overload in one affects the others.
